title: R' Shimon, son of R' Yannai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: R' Shimon son of R' Yannai. He is mentioned in [the Jerusalem Talmud, Shabbat ch. 13, halakhah 7](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.13.7.3), where he said: 'I did not hear this from my father; my sister told me in his name.' And there, [ch. 4, beginning of halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Shabbat.4.2.4): 'R-Sh b-R said: I did not hear this from my father' — Hyman regards this as a scribal error and says it should read R-Sh son of R' Yannai. And in [Moed Katan ch. 2, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Moed_Katan.2.2.2): Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi Yannai harvested

his vineyard during the intermediate days of the festival; all the people saw him and harvested after him; in the following year he left it, and it dried up. In [Moed Katan 12b](https://www.sefaria.org/Moed_Katan.12b.17) the incident is brought concerning R' Yannai, and Hyman writes that from this it appears that he was the son of the well-known R' Yannai, teacher of R' Yohanan, who as is known was wealthy and had vineyards. He is mentioned in [Esther Rabbah ch. 3, 12](https://www.sefaria.org/Esther_Rabbah.3.12); Song of Songs Rabbah ch. 4, locator פת; (and so it should read in Bereshit Rabbah, beginning of ch. 75); Midrash Tehillim

ch. 124, section 5. Hyman states that he also had a son named R' Yannai, who spoke in the name of his father, in Bereshit Rabbah end of ch. 81, [Vayikra Rabbah 21:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Vayikra_Rabbah.21.2). And we find in Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 175a: R' Yannai said in the name of R' Shimon son of R' Yannai: 248 iron hooks did the Holy One, blessed be He, place upon the 248 limbs a person has, etc. And this statement is brought in the Old Midrash Shmuel,

[end of ch. 21](https://www.sefaria.org/Midrash_Shmuel.21.3), and there it reads 'R' Yannai son of R' Shmuel bar R-Y'; Hyman says it should read 'of R' Shimon bar R-Y'. And in Yalkut Shmuel, remez 126, Hyman says it was copied mistakenly in the name of R' Shimon ben Yohai, when what was written was R-Sh-B-Y [abbreviation], and he is R' Shimon son of R' Yannai.

notes.text: Shabbat 13:7 names Shimon son of Rabbi Yannai, who says his sister told him in his father’s name. The Hebrew of Shabbat 4:2 has Shimon berabbi, with Yannai supplied in brackets in the accompanying English. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3482&lang=en) records the sister’s transmission and the vineyard episode.
Hyman’s proposed corrections distinguish Yannai son of Shimon, the Shmuel wording in Midrash Shmuel, and the Yalkut’s Shimon ben Yochai. The locator פת in Shir HaShirim Rabbah remains unresolved.

The Yerushalmi names Shimon son of Rabbi Yannai and says he let the vineyard dry in another year. The Bavli, at 12b beside Hyman’s 12a, names Rabbi Yannai and says he made the orchard ownerless. Hyman uses the comparison to infer which Rabbi Yannai was Shimon’s father.

Hyman’s printed notice spans vol. III, pp. 1191–1192. Vayikra Rabbah has Yannai speaking in the name of Shimon berabbi Yannai and gives the 248 iron hooks. The linked Midrash Shmuel has Yannai son of Shmuel bar Rabbi Yannai and gives fetters. Hyman proposes reading Shimon there and explains the Yalkut’s Shimon ben Yochai as a misreading of the abbreviation. The exact Pesikta pagination, Yalkut copying history, and the locator פת remain open.
